en: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system, and you could fit more than 1,300 Earths inside it.
The Moon is about 384,400 kilometers away from Earth, which is roughly equivalent to flying around the Earth's equator nine and a half times.
UY Scuti is one of the largest known stars, and if placed at the center of our solar system, its surface would extend beyond Jupiter's orbit.
Diamond is the hardest known natural mineral on Earth, scoring a perfect ten on the Mohs hardness scale used to measure scratch resistance.
The highest recorded temperature on Earth was 56.7 degrees Celsius in Death Valley, California, which is hot enough to boil water at lower altitudes.
One handful of healthy topsoil contains billions of microscopic organisms, including bacteria, fungi, and tiny insects that help break down dead plant matter.
About 97 percent of all water on Earth is salty ocean water, leaving only three percent as fresh water for drinking and farming.
The 1960 Valdivia earthquake in Chile is the most powerful earthquake ever recorded, measuring a massive 9.5 on the moment magnitude scale.
Antarctica is the coldest continent on Earth, holding the record for the lowest air temperature ever measured at minus 89.2 degrees Celsius.
Light from the Sun takes about eight minutes and twenty seconds to travel the 150 million kilometers to reach Earth.
The 1815 eruption of Mount Tambora in Indonesia was the most powerful volcanic eruption in recorded history, ejecting over 100 cubic kilometers of ash.
There are eight planets in our solar system, with four small, rocky inner planets and four large, gaseous outer planets called gas giants.
